caption:
Dust hides the middle of our galaxy.

The Milky Way is 13 billion years old and has gathered lots of dust.
Cosmic dust is far finer than couch dust. Dying stars release it into space.
In near-infrared light, dust soaks up the light and the centre is almost hidden.

What the astronomers say: mid-infrared light pierces the dust and reaches SPHEREx, close to why sunsets are red.

Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech SPHEREx; data from NASA/IPAC IRSA. Processing: The Bright Nobles (Muhammet Mücahit Soylu, Serdar Aydın, Furkan Küpeli), ChronosphereX.
